catalogue_requests.reason: no catalogue class sets the detector integration time of a spectrometer on its own: cap.device.configure.v1 would need it as writable state that a read returns, and Spectrometer has no getter for the integration time; cap.measure.spectrum.v1 couples the integration time to a full spectrum acquisition, whose output arrays need the artifact transport this package does not have. The capability sets the integration time persistently (Spectrometer.integration_time_micros) and reports the applied value.

notes:
The gate passed on the fake backend with no finding and no warning (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The card's decision is direct-driver, which this package follows: one decorated Driver over seabreeze.spectrometers:Spectrometer, the card's first entry symbol. Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware was attached, native.py was never imported and no spectrometer was opened or measured.

NOT COVERED. (1) The spectral array itself, the full wavelength/intensity arrays of all detector pixels, is not exposed. That array is what a spectrometer measures, and the standard has no artifact transport yet (cap.measure.spectrum.v1 expects an artifact_ref for large spectra), so the package exposes scalar intensity only and never returns the detector array; a reviewer who judges the array essential for this device should treat the package as NEEDS_ARTIFACTS rather than accept a truncated spectrum. (2) The card's GPIO, pixel-binning, optical-bench and Wi-Fi entry symbols are not exposed: in the pyseabreeze backend those classes are abstract definitions (module marked TODO, every method raises NotImplementedError, src/seabreeze/pyseabreeze/features/gpio.py:7), they are reached through the device feature dictionary rather than through Spectrometer, and cap.actuation.gpio.v1 binds io.gpio/io.digital, which an instrument.spectrometer resource does not declare. (3) The trigger mode is not exposed: the class documents its value as device-datasheet specific (src/seabreeze/spectrometers.py:344-351) and has no getter that would report an applied mode. (4) The card's candidate classes cap.sensing.read.v1 and cap.actuation.gpio.v1 were not used because they bind sensor and io resource kinds; cap.measure.intensity.v1 binds instrument.spectrometer and is the class this package uses.

FAKE SIZE. The fake's detector has 16 pixels and a fixed calibration (placeholder test data, marked # placeholder in fake.py); a real spectrometer returns the pixel count its model declares, e.g. spectrum_num_pixel = 2048 for USB2000PLUS/FLAMES (src/seabreeze/pyseabreeze/devices.py:506) and other counts for other models. Every receipt of this driver carries a scalar intensity, so no array of the device crosses the boundary; the fake's array is internal test data only.

BOUNDS. Two operator_required bounds: the integration time (the clone declares it per spectrometer model and the class reads it from the device at runtime) and the wavelength (the detector calibration is read at runtime). No line of the clone states one range for the device, so site-limits.example.json shows the overlay an operator supplies; until then every call carrying either field is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. fixtures/conformance.json pins the class action's probe input to the empty object because the class example carries those two operator-required fields and the driver's state read is taken without an operator overlay.

SAFETY. The device of this package measures and actuates nothing; the e-stop calls Spectrometer.close (src/seabreeze/spectrometers.py:413-414), the only native stop the class has, which ends an acquisition by closing the device connection. Risk is the card's floor R1, so no independent hardware e-stop is cited (SAFE-045 applies at R2 and above) and the hardware backend stays a human decision to enable.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted as a scalar driver (the intensity at one wavelength, the detector's scalar reads and the integration time); the spectrum array is not covered until the standard carries artifacts (PROMPT.md rule 4). The reviewer changed no file of the package. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
